extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, litigators, and judges handling patent disputes in Brazil
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for conducting patent-related civil actions in Brazilian courts, covering joinder, suspension, pleadings, case management, evidence (expert and testimonial), confidentiality, and alternative dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection/joinder of actions (continência)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 55 of the CPC, two or more actions are considered connected when they have a common request or cause of action; cases that risk rendering conflicting or contradictory decisions if decided separately may also be joined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder requires that none of the cases have yet been decided. Connection permits joint decision where separate rulings could conflict. (Article 55 CPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder where broader relief embraces others (Article 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases may be joined when there is identity of parties and cause of action but the relief sought in one case, being broader, embraces the relief sought in the other cases (Article 56 CPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides for joining related claims even where requests differ in scope, so long as one encompasses the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder and prevention jurisdiction (Articles 58–59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder of separately filed actions takes place in the court that obtained jurisdiction by prevention; filing or assignment of the oldest complaint to the court is considered to obtain prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevention (priority of filing/assignment) determines which court will hear joined actions (Articles 58–59 CPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inability to join federal nullity and state damages actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Although patent nullity actions and actions for damages may be connected, they cannot be joined due to the absolute jurisdiction of federal (nullity) and state (damages) courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State courts with jurisdiction over damages may suspend proceedings if they find an external priority; separate jurisdictions limit joinder despite substantive connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when dependent on another case (Article 313 V(a)–(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A case is suspended when its judgment on the merits depends on the judgment of another case or on verification/production of a fact/evidence requested by another court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During suspension, practicing procedural acts is forbidden though the judge may order execution of urgent acts to avoid irreparable damage (Article 314 CPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when civil proceedings depend on criminal verification (Article 315)
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil proceedings may be suspended at the judge's discretion if merits depend on verification of a criminal offense; if criminal action not filed within three months suspension ceases; if filed, suspension lasts up to one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At end of suspension (or lapse), the civil judge examines priority issues incidentally (Article 315 CPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy does not affect illiquid or nullity actions (Law No. 11,101 Art. 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declaration of bankruptcy or court-supervised reorganization does not affect processing of actions demanding illiquid amounts or requests for declaration of nullity; such actions continue with the judge assigned as if no bankruptcy existed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a bankrupt company is sentenced for infringement, the creditor must file a proof of claim within the bankruptcy procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint must state theories, facts, and documentary evidence (Articles 319, 320, 434, 141)
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint initiates the lawsuit and must indicate legal theories, factual circumstances, and existing documentary evidence at the first opportunity; requests delimit the judge's cognizance and judge cannot rule beyond what is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory attachments for patent plaintiffs: power of attorney, articles of incorporation, proof of payment of costs, foreign party power of attorney (if applicable), proof of security deposit (when required), letters patent, licenses, registrations, and priority receipts. Exceptional admission of subsequent documents only under specific articles (Art. 435, Art. 473(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: No pre-filing evidentiary or construction stage (Article 347)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brazilian law provides no preparatory phase before filing for parties to present evidence and theories; statements of case occur within the court process after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must include all legal theories and important facts in complaint/answer to avoid preclusion; dialogue between parties occurs under judicially regulated procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of plaintiff's request and preclusion rules (Article 329)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff may change the request or cause of action until service of process without defendant’s consent; after service changes require defendant’s consent until pre-trial order; after pre-trial order plaintiff can no longer change the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant bears burden of specific objection; parties should draft pleadings diligently to avoid losing rights by preclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's answer obligations and consequences of failure (Articles 335–342, 336, 341)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant must object to all aspects alleged in the complaint under penalty of preclusion; facts alleged by plaintiff and not objected to are considered true; failure to present defense leads to loss of burden to object and facts being deemed undisputed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant may raise procedural defenses (lack of jurisdiction, parallel litigation, arbitration agreement, standing, etc.). If defendant presents facts that modify/defeat plaintiff's rights, they must meet the same standard of reasoning and proof allocation (Article 373).

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterclaim requirements and procedure (Article 343)
rubrics_metrics.description: During the 15-business-day answer term defendant may file requests against plaintiff (counterclaims), which must be connected to the main action or ground of defense, comply with complaint assumptions, and require plaintiff's standing to be sued; counterclaims are treated similarly to separate cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plaintiff is summoned to answer within 15 days; withdrawal or extinction of main action does not prevent continuation of counterclaim (Article 343).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge's case management powers (Article 139 I–X)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge must ensure equal treatment, reasonable duration, prevent dilatory acts, determine coercive measures, promote resolution by parties, extend procedural terms and change evidence order, exercise police power, order personal presence, determine procedural compliance, and notify public bodies in repeated individual claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These powers authorize active judicial management to promote efficiency, fairness, and timeliness in patent cases; Article 139 sole paragraph limits term extensions to before the regular term ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case management tools available to judge
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools available include referral to conciliation/mediation, pre-trial order, trial hearing, procedural flexibility, scheduling of acts and terms, extension of dilatory terms, change in evidence production order, use of expert evidence (traditional, informal, out-of-court), and procedural legal transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling (Article 191) and procedural agreements (Article 190) are innovations in CPC/2015 to tailor process to case needs; calendars are binding and only exceptionally modified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' duties of good faith and cooperation (Articles 5–6) and obligation to plead all issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must act in good faith and cooperate; they are compelled to allege all possible issues in complaint/answer to avoid preclusion; procedural adequacy and necessity affect ability to bring claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because procedural costs and public nature discourage early settlement, parties should carefully present all theories and evidence early in the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and reallocation of burden of proof (Article 373 and Paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: General rule: burden of proof is incumbent on plaintiff for facts constituting his/her right, and on defendant for facts preventing/modifying/extinguishing plaintiff's right; judge may reassign burden by reasoned decision where necessary, except where impossible or excessively difficult or where it would affect unwaivable rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reallocation requires reasoned decision and opportunity for party to claim discharge; agreement between parties may reallocate burden except for unwaivable rights or where it makes exercising a right excessively difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trial order organizes the case and limits issues (Article 357)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pre-trial order marks end of pleading stage, defines disputed factual and legal points, assigns burden of proof, determines evidence to be produced, and remedies procedural defects; after it pleadings and requests generally cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge may order production of decisive evidence first if it may fully define outcome; judge exclusively defines points subject to evidentiary stage, usually factual rather than purely legal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary proceedings do not apply to patents (Article 318)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent lawsuits are governed by ordinary procedure; summary proceedings are inapplicable. However, if judgment can be rendered solely on documentary evidence in the record, judge may decide without additional evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not expect accelerated summary procedures for patent disputes but may obtain decisions on the pleadings when documentary record suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert evidence: appointment, role, and report contents (Articles 465, 473, 475)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert evidence is typically appointed by the judge; parties may agree on another expert and may appoint technical assistants. Experts' reports must include exposition of subject matter, technical/scientific analysis, indication of method used (accepted by specialists), and conclusive answers to all posed questions (Article 473).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts do not bind judges. Judges may appoint multiple experts for complex matters; experts and assistants must be registered; experts may be replaced for lack of competence or failure to comply. Parties can object to experts within 15 days and submit questions; judge may dismiss impertinent questions. Simplified expert opinions (state-of-the-art briefs) are permitted at judge's discretion to reduce cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert evidence procedure and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Experts must deliver reports within periods set by judge and at least 20 days before trial; parties may comment within a common 15-day term; court expert must clarify points within 15 days if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If clarification insufficient, judge can order new expert analysis or summon experts/assistants to trial. Number of questions to expert is not legally limited but may be objected to if beyond disputed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimonial evidence: witness lists and limits (Articles 357(6)–(7), 450–463, 459)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convenience of testimonial evidence is set by judge at pre-trial order; list of witnesses presented at least before trial; legislation limits maximum number of witnesses. Questions are asked by parties; judge disallows leading, irrelevant, or repetitive questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge may question witnesses before or after parties; parties should justify need for testimonial evidence and respect procedural limits on witnesses and questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of proceedings (Article 189 CPC; Article 206 LPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural acts are public, but proceedings are processed closed to the public in specific cases (public/social interest, family matters, privacy-protected data, arbitration-related matters). A request to close proceedings must state grounds and is appealable; Article 206 LPI requires closure when confidential industrial/commercial secrets are disclosed in court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proceedings are closed, record consultation is restricted to parties and attorneys; misuse of disclosed confidential information is prohibited. In search and seizure for process-patent crimes, court officer is accompanied by an expert to preliminarily verify illicit act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative dispute resolution: conciliation and mediation (CPC Article 334; Law No. 13,140/15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary procedure provides for a conciliation/mediation hearing soon after filing (Article 334 CPC); judges may adopt ADR at any time. Mediation (Law 13,140/15) is a confidential, technical activity by an impartial third party without decision-making power and may be used for waivable or negotiable rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mediators are appointed by court or chosen by parties and must meet minimum qualifications; courts maintain registries. Mediation confidentiality is broad (Article 14 Law 13,140/15) and mediated agreements, once approved by judge, are enforceable as court instruments. Compensation for court mediators set by courts and borne by parties.
